info.title: Digby API
info.description: Generated from the Express route definitions by `npm run openapi:generate` (backend/scripts/generate-openapi.ts). Do not hand-edit — regenerate after adding or changing routes; the openapi drift-guard test enforces freshness. Route metadata only (methods, paths, auth posture) — request/response schemas are intentionally not captured.

get.description:
Routes — ALL admin-only (this is the admin user-management module; a normal
user edits their OWN profile via /crossmodel profile endpoints, never here).
PUT /:id accepts `role` + `email`, so leaving it non-admin was a privilege-
escalation + account-takeover hole (2026-07-21 pre-launch audit). Every read
also exposes all users' PII, so list/get are admin-only too.
Requires the ADMIN role.

get.description:
The public page's figures load from here (generate_image tranche B, 2026-09-24):
the handler re-applies getSharedChat's link checks (exists + active + unexpired,
never a coding chat) and binds the GeneratedFile to the chat (owner AND chatId)
before serving inline with nosniff + public caching. Anything else is a 404 —
never a 415/410 that would confirm a file or link exists.

Shared canvas ARTIFACT — served as a real web page (HTML runs sandboxed).
One backend route serves every chat's artifacts straight from the DB row —
deliberately NOT per-project containers (service-sprawl future-proofing).

P4: RETIRED in favor of the ONE chat run stream, GET /api/crossmodel/chats/:id/stream
(crossmodel.routes.ts — it resolves both live-run key forms, so a coding run
attaches exactly as before). 308 preserves the method AND we preserve the
full query string verbatim: `?token=` (EventSource auth) and the back-compat
`?message=` run-start both keep working through the new endpoint.

Express 5 / path-to-regexp v8: a bare '*' wildcard is rejected — it must be
named (/*splat). The tail then arrives as string[] in req.params.splat.

build 2026-10-08 ISO — the credential proxy (coding/credential-proxy.ts).
Sandboxes call it with a session-bound capability (X-Digby-Cap), never a
user JWT, so it lives here (before the app-level guard) and authenticates
per request. A request without a valid capability is a uniform 401; the
upstream allowlist is fixed (git smart-HTTP to github.com; the GitHub /
Google / Slack / Asana API hosts). Inert until CODING_CREDENTIAL_PROXY
mints a capability for some run.
Literal paths (the openapi scanner reads string literals) = PROXY_ROUTE_PREFIX + …

get.description:
RELAY DATA PLANE — the DEVICE half (ticket c468f922, owner ruling
2026-10-29/30). These are the device's dial-OUT: it polls us, we never dial
it, and no inbound port exists on the Mac/PC. Agent-token auth like the poll
above; the session is resolved FROM the device's own grant, never named by
it. Registered before the JWT routes so an agent request can never be asked
for a user token.

delete.description:
Multi-Mac device management (owner 2026-09-24): per-device unpair / rename /
make-default. `authenticate` middleware scopes every handler to req.user.id —
the service layer additionally filters rows by { id, userId } so a forged id
can never touch another user's Mac.

patch.summary: Rename agent

post.description:
Permission onboarding buttons (ticket 2f646c10, agent ≥ 0.6.0): relaunch the
helper (post-update TCC self-heal), open a Privacy & Security pane, or reveal
the DigbyHelper binary in Finder.

BROKERED OPERATOR SESSION (ticket c468f922, owner ruling 2026-10-29 — the
"strong per-session auth" property): open / use-once / close a time-boxed
session bound to ONE device. Same `authenticate` + per-row userId scoping as
the device-management routes above, so a forged id can never touch another
user's Mac. Open is additionally gated on the remote-access verdict being
`ready`, so a session cannot be minted onto an exposed or half-configured
channel. The USE verb is what makes `stale` reachable: without a producer the
Redis key the verdict reader consults was never written by anything.

RELAY DATA PLANE — the OPERATOR half (ticket c468f922, owner ruling
2026-10-29/30): send / drain one session's frames. Same `authenticate` + the
per-row userId scoping as the grant verbs above, PLUS the session capability
minted when the session was opened — a sessionId alone never carries traffic,
because a JWT outlives any one session while a capability does not.

get.description:
OPERATOR-SIDE RENDERER (ticket c468f922) — the surface that turns carried
bytes back into something the operator can look at and act on. The two
verbs above CARRY a session; these two RENDER it (`…/relay/screen`) and
drive it (`…/relay/input`). Same `authenticate` + per-row userId scoping and
the same per-session capability in the x-session-capability header.
Kept in a separate controller module (relay-operator.controller.ts) because
`agent-derail-break.9cc62eef.test.ts` pins ABSOLUTE line windows of
imessage.controller.ts; see that module's header.

Progressive twin of /tts for read-aloud: each ≤600-char sentence chunk is
flushed as its own NDJSON line the moment it synthesizes (bounded
concurrency), so playback starts after the FIRST chunk instead of after the
whole answer. Lines: {"type":"chunk"|"done"|"error"|"ping", …} — the client
concatenates/plays by `index`. Keepalive pings every 20 s ride nginx's idle
timer. Body: { text: string, voice?: string }
